scaleGrammar.layout: whitespace/newline between figure and scale; punctuation after ; ) , ( tolerated
currencyForms: currency word suffix (720 million dollars / euros / pounds)
notMatched: bare '720 million' (no currency) is not an AMOUNT to the verifier - never MONEY by inference
'AND 100%' (ISO branch is case-sensitive and a figure followed by % is never an amount)

fix.currencyHandling: carried, never converted; two stated different currencies never match (NOT_ACCOUNTED_FOR with the currency named, IR side IR_ONLY); a side with no stated currency (IR NUMBER node, pre-F-3 inventory) keeps the pre-existing magnitude-only contract
fix.dimensionHandling: AMOUNT / PERCENT / RATIO kinds unchanged and never cross-compared; IR NUMBER nodes continue to inventory as AMOUNT (pre-existing contract, preserved and documented) so a MONEY literal the compiler emitted as a bare NUMBER still reconciles on magnitude
fix.arithmetic: BigInt over decimal digits x integer multiplier, divided exactly by 10^fractionDigits; exact:true within Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; comparison keeps reconciliation.ts's relative tolerance 1e-6 (float noise only; canonical values are exact integers)
fix.independenceDesign: B. fully independent parsing implementations - the verifier reads the raw source text with its own grammar (amount-parser.ts) and never consumes the compiler's normalized number; it deliberately mirrors the source system's intentional scale vocabulary without sharing code, and is stricter (single-letter abbreviations withheld for review). Independence stays meaningful because both sides must independently arrive at the same canonical figure from different evidence (source text vs composed IR) before anything is ACCOUNTED_FOR; the mechanical import-boundary test (semantic-verification-independence) still passes
